meta.title: Rust migration
meta.description: Migrates TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, PHP or C# code to Rust, one function or a whole app: the engine records the original's behavior and reports differences while the agent writes the port. Every language has a bridge (napi-rs or wasm, PyO3, a C ABI, cgo, Fiddle, JNI, PHP FFI, P/Invoke); the PHP bridge takes top-level functions only, and --batch is unavailable for PHP and C#. Analyze and bridge are verified here for all nine, and replaying PHP, C# or Kotlin needs that language's own toolchain. Ask to migrate code or to make one hot path faster. Read-only analyze and map run immediately; the other 20 engine tools (bridge, record, build, diff, bench, gate, go and more) write files or run project code, so each call needs one fresh approval. Recording and replay execute the target app and builds need its own toolchain, so use trusted projects that already build. Adds the rust-anything skill, a migration playbook (compile errors, FFI review, crate fit) and two prompt templates. Engine 3.3.0 is bundled for Windows x64; macOS and Linux need DSH_RUST_ANYTHING_BIN set to the absolute path of a trusted 3.3.0 executable. Timeouts and output limits are DSH_RUST_ANYTHING_* host settings. Disabling removes the tools, prompts and skill.
